fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY points DESC, wins DESC, person) AS finish` was computed inside the single SQL query that also contained the person-name `WHERE` filter. So when a user searched for a player by name, `finish` reflected rank within the filtered subset (e.g. the top match got rank 1) rather than their true position in the full leaderboard.

## What changed

**`decksite/data/competition.py`** — `load_leaderboard()` now accepts an `outer_where: str = 'TRUE'` parameter. The aggregation and `ROW_NUMBER()` are computed in an inner subquery (with only structural filters: competition_id, competition_series_id, season). The outer query wraps that subquery, applies `outer_where`, and computes `COUNT(*) OVER ()` for the filtered total. `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` also move to the outer query so pagination over the filtered set is correct.

**`decksite/controllers/api.py`** — The person-name text filter (`q`) is now built as `outer_where` and passed to the new parameter. Structural filters (competition_id, competition_series_id) remain in the inner `where`, keeping them inside the subquery so they properly scope the ROW_NUMBER computation.

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (no issues on touched files)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 848 passed, 1 skipped in 18.28 s (full suite, MariaDB running locally)

Fixes #7933

The text search filter `clauses.text_match_where(query.person_query(), q)` is merged into the same `where` string as competition_id/season filters, all passed to load_leaderboard() as the inner WHERE clause — so the ROW_NUMBER window function sees only the filtered rows
